summary.text: Zooxanthellae are photosynthetic single-celled organisms that live in symbiosis with marine invertebrates such as corals, jellyfish, sponges and nudibranchs.
By day they pass products of photosynthesis to their host, sometimes meeting up to 90% of its energy needs for metabolism, growth and reproduction.
In return they receive nutrients, carbon dioxide and a raised spot with access to sunlight, and their pigments give many hosts a yellowish or brownish colour.

facts.label: Energy supplied
facts.value: Up to 90% of the host's needs

facts.label: Hosts beyond corals
facts.value: Sea anemones, jellyfish, giant clams, sponges, flatworms

items.prompt: Living inside a host animal, up to what share of its energy needs can zooxanthellae supply?

options.label: About 5%
About 30%
Up to 90%
Always exactly 100%

items.explain: Through photosynthesis they sometimes provide up to 90% of the host's energy for metabolism, growth and reproduction.

items.prompt: A coral full of zooxanthellae is kept in a completely dark tank. What do its partners lose the ability to do?

options.label: Swim from one coral to another
Make food for the coral by photosynthesis
Absorb carbon dioxide from the coral
Build the coral's hard skeleton

items.explain: Zooxanthellae are photosynthetic, and the food they give their host comes from photosynthesis, which needs sunlight.

items.prompt: Zooxanthellae feed their host. What does the host give them back?

options.label: Nutrients, carbon dioxide and access to sunlight
Oxygen and a dark place to hide from light
Ready-made sugars from the host's meals
Nothing; they are parasites of the host

items.explain: In return for photosynthesis products, they receive nutrients, carbon dioxide and an elevated position with access to sunlight.

items.prompt: How did zooxanthellae first come to live inside host cells?

options.label: They forced their way in as parasites
They grew out of the host's own cell parts
Hosts farmed them on their outer skin first
Hosts took them in but failed to digest them

items.explain: Host cell lysosomes took them up, but instead of being broken down they survived because they supplied carbon compounds to the host.

items.prompt: Many corals and sea anemones look yellowish or brown. Where do those colours mostly come from?

options.label: Mud and sand stuck to the animal
Rust from iron dissolved in seawater
Pigments in the zooxanthellae inside them
The host's own blood showing through

items.explain: Zooxanthellae contain pigments such as peridinin and diadinoxanthin that give the yellowish and brownish colours typical of many hosts.

items.prompt: Zooxanthellae are best known from reef corals. Which of these other animals also hosts them?

options.label: The giant clam Tridacna
The great white shark
The green sea turtle
The bottlenose dolphin

items.explain: Besides reef-building corals, their hosts include sea anemones, jellyfish, nudibranchs, sponges, flatworms and bivalves such as the giant clam Tridacna.
